newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet body approves plan on VAT refunds.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet body approves plan on VAT refunds.

text.p: The Polish government's economic committee (KERM) approved on Wednesday a draft bill that would allow tourists leaving the country get a refund of value added tax on goods bought in Poland.

The government's press office said in a statement, the bill would allow both to bring Polish regulations closer to those of the European Union and help reduce the so-called grey untaxed sphere of the economy. @

It said the introduction of a VAT refund for travellers from countries which offer such refunds to Poles would be in line with Poland's association agreement with the EU which stresses the need to harmonise tax regulations.

It also said the refund would boost purchases of Polish goods and bring in more foreign currencies. It would also encourage some small firms to leave the shadow economy because only registered VAT taxpayers could offer the refunds.
Poland levies 22 percent VAT on most products.
Finance Minister Marek Belka earlier said the bill should come into force next year.
